page: Microsoft Azure D16pls_v5 is an arm64 virtual machine instance powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated physical cores mapped one-to-one to 16 vCPUs, alongside 32.0 GB of total RAM, translating to 2.0 GB per core. The cache structure consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This server does not bundle local disk storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage options.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded execution across dedicated cores, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 9624.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 28902.52. Memory bandwidth tests yield 126.1 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 67.32 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-thread performance shows lower comparative output, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1111.0, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 8.82 GB/sec, and encryption throughput at 2592.32. Application-level performance remains balanced, achieving 21.72 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.76 GB/sec in static web serving.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration, the hardware prioritizes processing density over memory footprint. This makes the architecture cost-effective for CPU-centric tasks that do not demand extensive working memory per thread or x86-specific vector extensions. Workloads aligned with this balance include continuous integration pipelines, software compilation tasks, static web serving, and horizontal microservice architectures.

The architecture features single-threaded cores without simultaneous multithreading, providing 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It contains no bundled local disks or hardware accelerators, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark testing indicates solid multi-core parallel efficiency, reaching 28902.52 in stress-ng and 21.72 million Redis SET operations per second, offset by lower single-threaded scores. The instance is well matched for distributed web serving, software compilation pipelines, container workloads, and parallel batch tasks.
